column1: text
Kerry Accuses Bush of Hiding the Truth About Iraq. Senator Kerry leveled his charges in a speech before the National Guard Association in Las Vegas.
Putin's Power Play. Russian President Vladimir Putin announced the biggest shake-up of Russia's political system since its 1993 adoption of a post-Soviet constitution.
Chinese in the dark as leaders gather. Citizens say they don't know anything about the leadership struggles, as the information isn't in the newspapers.
Australian rower Oliver goes slap-happy. Australia's women's rowing team was hit by scandal when Catriona Oliver walked up to teammate Sally Robbins and slapped her shoulder.
West Virginia's task: Climb over Maryland. West Virginia football coach Rich Rodriguez's thoughts turned to this weekend's opponent after dispatching Central Florida.
Woods to play at 84 Lumber Classic. The battle for number one between Vijay Singh and Tiger Woods is coming to western Pennsylvania.
LSU-Auburn Rivalry Could Get New Chapter. Auburn and LSU have played several nickname games in recent years: The Fire Game, The Interception Game, The Cigar Game.
Ohio State Buckeyes Succeed in Close Games. Ohio State is 15-5 in games decided by a touchdown or less under coach Jim Tressel, an uncanny run of success.
Kerry and Bush running neck and neck in White House race. As the convention-time boost for Bush waned, he and Kerry were again running neck and neck less than two months before the election.
Kids create new sign language. A new sign language created over 30 years by deaf Nicaraguan children gives a unique insight into how languages evolve.
British ambassador visits DPRK blast site. British Foreign Office minister Bill Rammell said the ambassador has visited the site of a huge explosion that raised fears.
Weekly Report On Israeli Human Rights Violations. Israeli Occupation Forces have perpetrated more human rights violations against Palestinian civilians.
Bonds 3-For-3 But No Homer, Remains at 699. Barry Bonds went 3-for-3 with a walk but failed to hit his 700th career home run as the Giants beat the Brewers 4-0.
Irish Help European Team at Ryder Cup. The Americans have the big names. The Europeans have the luck of the Irish.
Europe Strikes Early Ryder Blow with Charm Offensive. Holders Europe gained an early Ryder Cup advantage by winning over the home fans at Oakland Hills.
Teams United in Desire to Wait for Players in Labor Dispute. NHL teams appeared united in their determination to solve the league's economic problems as the lockout became official.
State Dept. Official Arrested in Inquiry on Taiwan Contact. The Foreign Service officer is suspected of improperly passing documents to Taiwanese intelligence agents.
Donors examine billions of dollars in aid for Iraq. Donors to Iraq's reconstruction are examining billions of dollars in aid pledges that have gone mostly unused amid an insurgency.
Prince Sihamoni to be named new king of Cambodia. Prince Norodom Sihamoni will be named king of Cambodia by the nine-member Throne Council.
Officer probe as girl shot dead in Gaza. The Israeli army suspended a platoon commander accused of emptying an ammunition clip into a 13-year-old Palestinian girl.
Election monitors weigh complaints in Afghanistan. Foreign election experts studied complaints from candidates in Afghanistan's first-ever presidential election.
Japan Fumes Over Whales as U.N. Meeting Winds Up. Japan was fuming over the failure of its bid to expand trade in whale products at a U.N. meeting.
Armitage: US Not Yet Seeking Sanctions on Iran. Washington is open to ideas other than taking Iran to the UN Security Council for sanctions over its nuclear program.
China sports star in AIDS campaign. AIDS activists get help from Chinese basketball star Yao Ming, back in Shanghai for a promotional game.
Plane diverted in security alert. A plane flying from Hong Kong to London's Heathrow airport is diverted to Stansted following a security alert.
Taiwan said to conduct plutonium tests in the 1980s. The UN nuclear watchdog agency found that Taiwan's experiments with plutonium extended to the mid-1980s.
Worker rights, welfare demands fail in Hong Kong. Newly elected lawmakers threw out two motions calling for more workers' rights and welfare.
Narrow rule feared after Russia lifts leader limits. The Duma voted to overturn a ban on political party leaders becoming ministers, raising fears of one-party rule.
China dismisses Taiwan overture. The Chinese government declared that a conciliatory proposal by Taiwan's president was fraudulent.
Egypt eyes possible link of 17 arrests to Sinai bombings. Egyptian authorities are investigating whether 17 suspected Al Qaeda members have any connection with the Sinai bombings.
Russian rocket blasts off for station. A Russian rocket carrying a new crew to the international space station lifted off from the Baikonur cosmodrome.
Officials target support for foreign fighters in Iraq. Six US soldiers were reported killed while the prime minister threatened an offensive against Fallujah.
Blair says he won't apologize for Iraq war. Prime Minister Tony Blair denied he misled Britain over Iraqi weapons and refused to apologize for the war.
Sharp Contrasts for Candidates on Domestic and Social Issues. Bush and Kerry clashed over terrorism, job losses, and health care in the presidential debates.
Justices Consider Executions of Young Killers. The court appeared deeply divided over whether the death penalty for juvenile acts should be seen as cruel and unusual punishment.
FDA Approves Use of Chip in Patients. Privacy advocates are concerned that an implantable microchip designed for medical records could undermine confidentiality.
New Crew Sets Off for Space Station. A Russian rocket carrying two cosmonauts and an American astronaut to the space station lifted off from Baikonur.
US pushes NATO over Afghanistan. The US is calling on NATO to take overall responsibility for peacekeeping and reconstruction in Afghanistan.
Els won't bow to USPGA. World number 2 Ernie Els is fuming after receiving demands from the American Tour that he must play more tournaments in the US.
Sub hits US hat-trick. United States, Mexico and Guatemala advanced to next year's World Cup qualifying final round with shutout triumphs.
Teenager joins the race for future NASCAR success. Next October, Chase Austin will finally be old enough to drive to the grocery store by himself.
Panthers' defense takes big hit before game with Eagles. Carolina Panthers' hopes of relying on their defense took a big hit with key injuries announced.
Beckham out for up to a month. David Beckham will be out of action for up to a month with the rib injury he suffered from his foul on Ben Thatcher.
Becks row rumbles on. David Beckham is still in danger of disciplinary action for admitting he got booked on purpose.
Australia elect to bat in second test against India. Stand-in captain Adam Gilchrist elected to bat in the second test with Australia leading the series 1-0.
Pujols Gets Cardinals Off to Fast Start. Albert Pujols made sure the St. Louis Cardinals got off to another fast start in the postseason.
Trail Blazers Clobber SuperSonics 92-73. Portland Trail Blazers opened preseason play with a 92-73 victory over the Seattle SuperSonics.
Boston Sluggers Fall Silent for 2nd Game. Red Sox bats that knocked balls over fences all season flailed wildly in the first two games of the championship series.
Soccer World Cup: U.S. Beats Panama 6-0. The United States advanced to the next round of World Cup qualifying with a game to spare.
Win Over Miami Would Be Big for Louisville. The spectator with divided loyalties will be Howard Schnellenberger at the Miami-Louisville game.
Yankees Edge Red Sox to Take Command of Series. Jon Lieber pitched seven shutout innings as the Yankees dumped the Red Sox 3-1 to take command of the ALCS.
Johnson's Sudden Hat Trick Leads U.S. Past Panama. Eddie Johnson came off the bench to score a hat-trick in 16 minutes as the U.S. thrashed Panama 6-0.
Kremlin Spins Putin's Proposed Plans. Following broad criticism that Putin is exploiting the Beslan school massacre, the Kremlin mobilized spokespeople.
NBA's young Bobcats add experience in Smith. The Charlotte Bobcats signed veteran shooting guard Steve Smith to bring experience to the expansion team.
NHL Talent Comes Home. Andrei Nazarov and Oleg Saprykin were supposed to be teammates for Phoenix but instead squared off in Russia.
Trulli Felt Bad Vibes at Monza. Toyota's new signing Jarno Trulli says being blamed for Renault losing second place sped up the driver switch.
MLB player arrested after brawl. A brawl erupted between fans and Texas Rangers players, resulting in pitcher Frank Francisco being arrested.
Bayer give a Real shock. Bayer Leverkusen hammered Real Madrid 3-0, the most stunning upset in the opening rotation of the Champions League.
Oil Up on Worries of Output Shut by Ivan. World oil prices rose on worries about oil production shut by Hurricane Ivan and a new approaching storm.
Respect Lebanon's sovereignty by respecting the Constitution. The sovereignty of Lebanon has suddenly become an issue of regional and global interest.
Gaza Gunmen Kidnap, Then Free Palestinian Official. Palestinian gunmen kidnapped a top security official they accused of corruption and held him for several hours.
Annan Calls for Urgent Action in Sudan. UN Secretary-General Kofi Annan called for urgent action to stop attacks on civilians in western Sudan.
Volatile Oil Prices Hold Stocks in Check. Stocks regained some momentum as fresh economic data suggested inflation remains under control.
Settlers or Sharon. Sharon is as far away as ever from recognizing the national rights of the Palestinian people.
Oakland Hills Now Seen As Golf Mecca. Oakland Hills' place in golf history was secure before the Ryder Cup arrived in Michigan.
Sprinter Earle Connor suspended from Paralympic team. Canadian sprinter has been suspended pending final review of his positive drug test.
Hughes to take Bowen with him to Blackburn. New Blackburn Rovers boss Mark Hughes is expected to take his Wales assistant Mark Bowen to Ewood Park.
Who's the Champ? Who Cares? NASCAR Wants TV Ratings. NASCAR begins its 10-race shootout for the Nextel Cup Championship in a new format.
Gold helmet winners: Shawn Brady leads Northeastern. With four touchdown passes in Northeastern's 34-30 win over Villanova, Brady was awarded the Gold Helmet.
BC stays in running with embarrassment of riches. When it comes to inexperienced, talented running backs, Boston College is blessed with options.
Down again in New York for the Red Sox. After a devastating loss in the Bronx, Red Sox management might want to decorate with black crepe.
European powers get back on track in World Cup qualifying. Order was restored while Brazil and Argentina were both held to goalless draws.
Celtics learn a lot in loss to Pistons. The Pistons returned to the scene of their championship triumph and hosted a learning experience for Boston.
Disgruntled Rice keeps up pressure for a trade. Jerry Rice met with Oakland Raiders owner Al Davis to discuss the receiver's future after requesting a trade.
Experience big in Phillies' search for new manager. Former Red Sox manager Grady Little is among five former managers interviewing for the vacant position.
BC High shuts down the Prep. Defense has been the theme for BC High and St. John's Prep, with BC High winning 1-0 to claim the conference title.
Johnson receives a message with benching. Bethel Johnson remains in the dark on why Patriots coach Belichick kept him off the active roster.
Hamas commander surrenders in his underwear. A terrorist commander surrendered meekly after Israeli paratroopers surrounded his West Bank hideout.
Israeli soldier suspended in girl's death. The Israeli army suspended a platoon commander suspected of shooting a 13-year-old Palestinian girl.
Huge Explosion Rocks Gaza City. A Palestinian schoolgirl runs past rubble of a destroyed building next to a United Nations school in Gaza.
Sharp Contrasts for Candidates. Bush and Kerry ended the debates with starkly defined differences on most domestic and foreign policy issues.
A Crucial Test, but Not Final. George W. Bush and John Kerry ended the debates as they began them, with starkly defined differences on most issues.
Justices deeply divided over juvenile death penalty. The Supreme Court appeared divided over whether executing those who committed crimes as juveniles is constitutional.
FDA approves implantable microchip for patients. Privacy advocates worry the chip designed for medical records could track patients' movements.
US pushes NATO to take charge in Afghanistan. The US is proposing that separate US and NATO missions in Afghanistan merge under NATO command.
Korean exchange programs face uncertainty. Educational exchanges between North and South Korea face new hurdles amid diplomatic tensions.
Australia chooses to bat in second cricket test against India. Captain Adam Gilchrist won the toss and chose to bat first in the second Test in Chennai.
Pujols leads Cardinals to fast postseason start. Albert Pujols ensured the St. Louis Cardinals began their postseason campaign with momentum.
Trail Blazers overcome preseason troubles with convincing win. After a camp marred by trouble, Portland opened preseason with a dominant 92-73 victory.
Red Sox bats go quiet in championship series. The powerful Boston offense that dominated all season went silent in the opening games against the Yankees.
US advances in World Cup qualifying with game to spare. Eddie Johnson's hat trick powered the United States past Panama 6-0 in CONCACAF qualifying.
Louisville eyes statement win over Miami. A victory over the third-ranked Hurricanes would boost Louisville's national profile significantly.
Yankees take commanding ALCS lead over Red Sox. Jon Lieber's seven shutout innings carried New York to a 3-1 victory and series control.
Soccer: Johnson hat-trick sinks Panama. Eddie Johnson needed just 16 minutes off the bench to score three goals as the US cruised to a 6-0 win.
NBA veteran Smith joins expansion Bobcats. Charlotte signed experienced guard Steve Smith to provide leadership for the first-year franchise.
NHL lockout becomes official as talks stall. The National Hockey League locked out its players as the two sides failed to resolve their economic dispute.
Ryder Cup: Europe charms Oakland Hills crowd. The European team won over American fans with their approach ahead of the biennial golf competition.
Wall Street Bears Claw Back Into the Black. Short-sellers, Wall Street's dwindling band of ultra-cynics, are seeing green again as markets decline.
Oil and Economy Cloud Stocks' Outlook. Soaring crude prices plus worries about the economy are expected to hang over the stock market next week.
Iraq Halts Oil Exports from Main Southern Pipeline. Authorities halted oil export flows after intelligence showed a rebel militia could strike infrastructure.
